| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
| Team | Up to 5 people. |

## How you're scored

Every scored run gets a quality and an eligibility verdict; the platform measures its cost and time.

- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.

Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.

Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.

On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.

#!/bin/sh
# Installs the Atira Challenges CLI for you alone, without sudo:
#   ~/.local/share/atira/atira.mjs   the CLI, checked against the platform's SHA-256 before it is kept
#   ~/.local/share/atira/node/       Node.js 24 for atira alone, only when this computer has no Node 24 (it asks first)
#   ~/.local/bin/atira               a wrapper: your node when it is 24 or newer, else the private one
# It never changes your PATH or the `node` on it. ATIRA_INSTALL_NODE=1 (or 0) answers the question without asking.
# Uninstall: rm -rf ~/.local/share/atira ~/.local/bin/atira   (and ~/.config/atira, the sign-in)
# Read it first: curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | less
set -eu

api="${ATIRA_API:-https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai}"
dist="${ATIRA_NODE_DIST:-https://nodejs.org/dist/latest-v24.x}"
share="$HOME/.local/share/atira"
bin="$HOME/.local/bin"
download="https://nodejs.org/en/download"

fail() {
  printf 'atira install: %s\n' "$1" >&2
  exit 1
}

# whether the node at $1 is version 24 or newer
node24() {
  v=$("$1" --version 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  v=${v#v}
  case ${v%%.*} in '' | *[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
  [ "${v%%.*}" -ge 24 ]
}

sha256() {
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1"
  elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then shasum -a 256 "$1"
  else openssl dgst -sha256 -r "$1"; fi | cut -d ' ' -f 1
}

command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "curl is needed to download the CLI."
command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1 || command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1 || command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
  fail "sha256sum, shasum or openssl is needed to check the downloads."

private=""
if ! { command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && node24 node; } && ! node24 "$share/node/bin/node"; then
  case $(uname -s) in
    Darwin) os=darwin ;;
    Linux) os=linux ;;
    MINGW* | MSYS* | CYGWIN*) fail "On Windows, install from PowerShell: irm $api/install.ps1 | iex" ;;
    *) fail "Node.js 24 or newer is needed. Install it from $download and run this again." ;;
  esac
  case $(uname -m) in
    x86_64 | amd64) arch=x64 ;;
    arm64 | aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "nodejs.org has no Node.js 24 for $(uname -m). Install Node.js 24 or newer yourself and run this again." ;;
  esac
  for musl in /lib/ld-musl-*; do
    if [ -e "$musl" ]; then
      fail "nodejs.org builds Node.js for glibc, and this Linux uses musl (Alpine, for one). Install Node.js 24 or newer with your package manager and run this again."
    fi
  done
  if [ -d "$share/node" ]; then
    answer=${ATIRA_INSTALL_NODE:-1} # a private copy you said yes to before, now too old or broken
  elif [ -n "${ATIRA_INSTALL_NODE:-}" ]; then
    answer=$ATIRA_INSTALL_NODE
  elif (: </dev/tty) 2>/dev/null; then
    if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf 'atira needs Node.js 24 or newer; this computer has %s.\n' "$(node --version 2>/dev/null)" >/dev/tty
    fi
    printf "Node.js 24 isn't available. Install a private copy for atira (no admin rights, ~/.local/share/atira/node)? [Y/n] " >/dev/tty
    read -r answer </dev/tty || answer=n
    case $answer in '' | [Yy] | [Yy][Ee][Ss]) answer=1 ;; *) answer=0 ;; esac
  else
    fail "Node.js 24 isn't available, and there is no terminal to ask whether to install a private copy for atira.
Install Node.js 24 or newer from $download and run this again, or let the script install a private copy
(no admin rights, ~/.local/share/atira/node; your PATH and node stay as they are):
  curl -fsSL $api/install.sh | ATIRA_INSTALL_NODE=1 sh"
  fi
  case $answer in
    1) private="$os-$arch" ;;
    0) fail "Nothing was installed. Install Node.js 24 or newer from $download and run this again." ;;
    *) fail "ATIRA_INSTALL_NODE must be 1 (install a private Node.js for atira) or 0 (don't)." ;;
  esac
fi

mkdir -p "$share" "$bin"
work=$(mktemp -d "$share/.install.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
trap 'exit 1' INT TERM

curl -fsSL "$api/cli.mjs" -o "$work/atira.mjs" || fail "Could not download $api/cli.mjs."
expected=$(curl -fsSL "$api/cli.mjs.sha256" | cut -d ' ' -f 1)
actual=$(sha256 "$work/atira.mjs")
[ -n "$expected" ] && [ "$expected" = "$actual" ] || fail "The download does not match its checksum; nothing was installed. Try again in a minute."

if [ -n "$private" ]; then
  format=gz # xz is half the size: when xz is there, or tar is bsdtar (macOS), which reads it without
  if command -v xz >/dev/null 2>&1 || tar --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q bsdtar; then format=xz; fi
  sums=$(curl -fsSL "$dist/SHASUMS256.txt") || fail "Could not download $dist/SHASUMS256.txt; nothing was installed."
  line=$(printf '%s\n' "$sums" | grep -E "^[0-9a-f]{64}  node-v24\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-$private\.tar\.$format\$" | head -n 1)
  [ -n "$line" ] || fail "$dist/SHASUMS256.txt lists no Node.js 24 for $private; nothing was installed."
  name=${line##* }
  printf 'Downloading %s from %s\n' "$name" "$dist"
  curl -fsSL "$dist/$name" -o "$work/$name" || fail "Could not download $dist/$name; nothing was installed."
  [ "$(sha256 "$work/$name")" = "${line%% *}" ] ||
    fail "$name does not match its SHA-256 in $dist/SHASUMS256.txt; nothing was installed."
  mkdir "$work/node"
  if [ $format = xz ]; then tar -xJf "$work/$name" -C "$work/node" --strip-components 1
  else tar -xzf "$work/$name" -C "$work/node" --strip-components 1; fi
  node24 "$work/node/bin/node" || fail "The Node.js from $dist does not run on this computer; nothing was installed."
  rm -rf "$share/node"
  mv "$work/node" "$share/node"
  printf 'Installed Node.js %s for atira alone: %s (sha256 %s)\n' "$("$share/node/bin/node" --version)" "$share/node" "${line%% *}"
fi

mv "$work/atira.mjs" "$share/atira.mjs"
cat > "$bin/atira" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh

# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

## Run it locally

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

Terminal 1: start the free models and leave it open.

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2, in this folder:

```sh
uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"     # the scouting logins, and the model variables pointed at that proxy
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

In PowerShell on Windows, Terminal 2:

```powershell
uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression    # the same exports
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

A Chromium window opens (`HEADLESS=1` hides it). Nothing done with the scouting logins counts, and locally an answer
is printed, never submitted. If `atira` says `Unknown command: models`, run `atira upgrade`.

## Test-run it, then submit it

```sh
atira test-run .   # the sandbox, exactly like a scored run, on the public dataset; opens the run page live
atira submit .     # reviewed, then run once and scored for the leaderboard
```

Both pack this directory without what `.gitignore` excludes.

## Environment

| Variable | Set by | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | runs | the run, at `/v1/runs/current` |
| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` | `atira scout --env` | locally: the brief and the scouting logins |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS` | runs | the sandbox's browsers; locally the kit starts its own Chromium |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env` | the hosted Qwen |
| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env`, when Clef is hosted | the hosted Clef |

# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

## Run it locally

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

Terminal 1: start the free models and leave it open.

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2, in this folder:

```sh
uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"     # the scouting logins, and the model variables pointed at that proxy
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

In PowerShell on Windows, Terminal 2:

```powershell
uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression    # the same exports
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

A Chromium window opens (`HEADLESS=1` hides it). Nothing done with the scouting logins counts, and locally an answer
is printed, never submitted. If `atira` says `Unknown command: models`, run `atira upgrade`.

## Test-run it, then submit it

```sh
atira test-run .   # the sandbox, exactly like a scored run, on the public dataset; opens the run page live
atira submit .     # reviewed, then run once and scored for the leaderboard
```

Both pack this directory without what `.gitignore` excludes.

| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | runs | the run, at `/v1/runs/current` |
